CLINICAL DETAILS: 66M. Known diverticular disease. 3 days of left iliac fossa pain, now generalised peritonism. Temp 38.6, CRP 287, lactate 2.4.

TECHNIQUE: CT abdomen and pelvis, portal venous phase, following intravenous contrast.

FINDINGS:
Extensive sigmoid diverticular disease with a 9 cm segment of sigmoid wall thickening and marked pericolic fat stranding. There are locules of extraluminal gas adjacent to the mid sigmoid with a 32 mm rim-enhancing pericolic collection, and free intraperitoneal gas beneath the anterior abdominal wall, in keeping with perforated diverticulitis. The remainder of the colon and the small bowel are not dilated. The appendix is unremarkable.

The liver, gallbladder and biliary tree are unremarkable.

The pancreas, spleen and adrenal glands are unremarkable.

The kidneys are unremarkable with no hydronephrosis. The bladder is unremarkable.

Free intraperitoneal gas as described above. Small volume of free fluid in the pelvis.

No lymphadenopathy. The abdominal aorta is of normal calibre.

The pelvic organs are unremarkable.

The lung bases are clear. No aggressive bone lesion.

CONCLUSION:
1. Perforated sigmoid diverticulitis with free intraperitoneal gas and a 32 mm pericolic collection.
Recommend urgent surgical review.
